item.text:
I would harden three places:

- [`averageItemPrice`](C:\Users\Kerim\AppData\Local\Temp\codex-eco-bench-Qj3OBM\test\orders.js#L18-L20): guard `items.length === 0` before dividing, or return `0`/`null`. Right now empty input produces `NaN`, which tends to leak into downstream calculations.
- [`calcTotal`](C:\Users\Kerim\AppData\Local\Temp\codex-eco-bench-Qj3OBM\test\orders.js#L3-L8): validate that `items` is an array and each item has numeric `price` and `qty`. Without that, bad data turns into `NaN` or runtime errors.
- [`formatOrder`](C:\Users\Kerim\AppData\Local\Temp\codex-eco-bench-Qj3OBM\test\orders.js#L22-L26): validate `order.items` and `order.discountCode` before formatting. This function assumes a fully shaped object and will fail or print misleading totals if the caller passes partial data.

I’d also tighten `applyDiscount` by rejecting unknown codes explicitly if invalid codes should not silently behave like no discount. That depends on business rules: silent fallback is safe for UX, but weak for correctness if discount codes are user-supplied.
